draft.title: What moves the plates
card: Tectonic plates move slowly, about a few centimetres a year. That is roughly the speed at which fingernails grow.
Convection
hot rock in the mantle rises, cools, then sinks, in a very slow loop. Plates ride on this flow and are carried along with it.
Ridge push
at a spreading ridge, new plate material is hot and sits high. Gravity makes it slide down the slope and push the plate away from the ridge.
Slab pull
where an old, cold plate sinks into the mantle, its weight drags the rest of the plate behind it.
draft.remember: Plates are moved by mantle convection, pushed from ridges and pulled by sinking slabs.

a.q: At a subduction zone, the edge of an old, cold plate sinks into the mantle and drags the rest of the plate along. What is this force called?
opts: Slab pull
Ridge push
Convection
Spreading
a.why: The sinking edge of the plate is a heavy slab, and its weight pulls the plate behind it. Ridge push is the tempting answer, but it happens at a spreading ridge, where gravity makes new plate slide away from the high ridge.
a.clue: Think about the weight of the sinking edge.

b.q: Dani says plates move because they push themselves along like cars. Which statement best corrects her?
opts: Plates are moved by mantle flow, ridge push and slab pull
Plates are moved only by the Moon pulling on the crust
Plates move quickly, so a plate travels metres each day
Plates are moved by wind and ocean currents at the surface
b.why: The card says plates are driven by convection in the mantle, ridge push and slab pull. The other options give wrong causes or a wrong speed, since plates move only a few centimetres a year.
b.clue: Check the three forces named on the card.

b.best: Plates are moved by mantle flow, ridge push and slab pull

problems.detail: The stem uses the term 'subduction zone', which the card never teaches. The rest of the stem explains it, so students can still answer, but the term is introduced without support.

The distractors (wind and ocean currents, metres each day, the Moon) are implausible. The clue 'Check the three forces named on the card' also points straight to the only option that lists three forces, so students can answer by matching words rather than understanding.

proposal.title: What moves the plates
card: Tectonic plates move slowly, about a few centimetres a year. That is roughly the speed at which fingernails grow.
Convection
hot rock in the mantle rises, cools, then sinks, in a very slow loop. Plates ride on this flow and are carried along with it.
Ridge push
at a spreading ridge, new plate material is hot and sits high. Gravity makes it slide down the slope and push the plate away from the ridge.
Slab pull
where an old, cold plate sinks into the mantle, its weight drags the rest of the plate behind it, towards the sinking edge.
proposal.remember: Plates can be carried by mantle flow, pushed away from ridges and pulled by sinking slabs.

a.q: The edge of an old, cold plate sinks into the mantle. Its weight drags the rest of the plate along. What is this force called?
opts: Slab pull
Ridge push
Mantle convection
Sea-floor spreading
a.why: The sinking edge is a heavy slab, and its weight pulls the plate behind it. Ridge push is the tempting answer, but it happens at a spreading ridge, where gravity makes new, high plate slide away from the ridge.
a.clue: Is the plate being pushed from behind or dragged from the front?

b.q: A plate has a spreading ridge along its west edge. Its east edge is old and cold and sinks into the mantle. How do ridge push and slab pull act on it?
opts: Both move it the same way, east towards the sinking edge
They act in opposite directions and cancel each other out
Ridge push moves it west, while slab pull moves it east
Only slab pull acts, as ridge push needs a sinking edge
b.why: Ridge push slides the plate away from the ridge, which is east. Slab pull drags the plate towards its sinking edge, which is also east. The two forces add together rather than cancel, so the option about opposite directions is wrong.
b.clue: Work out which way each force moves the plate on its own.

b.best: Both move it the same way, east towards the sinking edge
